blocks.text: Humanistic/Existential Review
Client Centered Therapy

Views people are always growing and inherently good. Avoids diagnosis, avoid strict adherence to what the ideal person should be. Role of therapist is nondirective, not steering client in any one direction (unlike CBT or systems theory). Driven by what the client wants to talk about. T is a facilitator who is helping the person to grow and change. This occurs by creating unconditional positive regard. Client determines the goals of therapy. Up to the client to decide how many sessions they would like as well, a lot of support for client self-determination.

blocks.text: Gestalt

The idea is that change occurs through increased awareness of here and now experience and dialogic relationship between T and client. Dialogic refers to a therapeutic stance where the therapist and client engage as two authentic human beings — fully present with each other, co-creating the therapeutic process. Heavily influenced by Martin Buber’s “I-Thou” philosophy, where the therapist meets the client as a fellow human, not an object to be treated.

blocks.text: Goals: client discovers their own life meaning, what does life mean to them, confront anxiety inherent in living. Anxiety is a part of the human condition, being able to deal with it effectively instead of getting rid of it. Agency: making their own choices in life, responsibility in the construction of their life. Emphasizes empowerment of the client. Self-awareness. Freedom. Each person has unique identity that can only be known through genuine relationships with others. It’s not until you encounter someone else that you can truly know yourself – this is why T must be a true other. Client experiences their own uniqueness through that. Each person must continually recreate themselves, life is always moving forward, existence is not fixed and we are always changing.

Theory of Change

Change happens through the existential encounter – the authentic meeting of the therapist and the client in the present moment and by expanding the client’s range of experience. Very influenced by Gestalt therapy. Generally used with families, started by Carl Whittaker.

blocks.text: Battle for Initiative: Motivation for change must come from family. Includes having a family state the agenda for each session, waiting silently for family to take initiative, allowing family to determine how change is going to happen. The therapist should not be working harder than the family. A family comes in, and nobody is speaking. What would experiential therapist do? The right answer would be the therapist would wait silently for the family to take initiative.
